nodes.summary: The imputed statistic `ẑ = wᵀ z_o` with weights `w`.
nodes.title: Imputed summary statistic

nodes.summary: If `Σ_oo w = Σ_ot`, then for any weights `w'`, `𝔼 (z_t - w'ᵀ z_o)² = 𝔼 (z_t - wᵀ z_o)² + (w' - w)ᵀ Σ_oo (w' - w)`.
nodes.title: Excess error of a linear imputation

nodes.summary: The weights solving `Σ_oo w = Σ_ot` minimize the mean squared error `𝔼 (z_t - w'ᵀ z_o)²` over all weights `w'`.
nodes.title: ImpG is the best linear imputation

nodes.summary: For the ImpG weights (`Σ_oo w = Σ_ot`) the mean squared imputation error is `Σ_tt - wᵀ Σ_ot = Σ_tt - Σ_to Σ_oo⁻¹ Σ_ot`, the linear-prediction residual variance (the conditional variance only under the Gaussian ImpG model).
nodes.title: Mean squared error of imputation with ImpG weights

nodes.summary: The mean squared imputation error: `𝔼 (z_t - ẑ)² = Σ_tt - 2 wᵀ Σ_ot + wᵀ Σ_oo w`.
nodes.title: Mean squared imputation error
Cross moment of the imputed and untyped statistics

nodes.summary: For the ImpG weights (`Σ_oo w = Σ_ot`, i.e. `w = Σ_oo⁻¹ Σ_ot` when `Σ_oo` is invertible) the imputed statistic has second moment `wᵀ Σ_ot = Σ_to Σ_oo⁻¹ Σ_ot`; for `Σ_tt = 1` this is `1 -` the linear-prediction residual variance, ImpG's `r²_pred`.
nodes.title: Second moment of the statistic imputed with ImpG weights
Second moment of the imputed statistic

nodes.summary: For any weights `w` with `wᵀ Σ_oo w > 0` (for example the ridge weights solving `(Σ_oo + λ I) w = Σ_ot`), the statistic `ẑ / √(wᵀ Σ_oo w)` has second moment `1`, so it has unit variance under the centred null.
nodes.title: Normalized imputed statistic

nodes.summary: Square-integrable statistics `z_t` (untyped marker) and `z_o` (typed markers) with raw second moments `𝔼 z_o z_oᵀ = Σ_oo`, `𝔼 z_t z_o = Σ_ot`, `𝔼 z_t² = Σ_tt`. These are the covariances of the ImpG null model when the statistics are centred.
nodes.title: Second-moment model for summary-statistic imputation

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
